A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Ada-KV work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original LongBench evaluations, Needle-in-a-Haystack retrieval experiments, attention analyses, and memory and latency measurements.

after.justification: v4 reports original RULER and LongBench evaluations under question-aware and question-agnostic conditions, alongside attention analyses and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The global Top-k budget allocation, safeguard mixing, and SnapKV/Pyramid integrations remain. v4 Section 3.5 introduces GQA-compatible eviction using mean attention weights within each group to preserve shared KV caches, a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v4 retains the 16 LongBench datasets and adds 13 RULER tasks, extending retrieval requirements to multiple keys, values, and queries, variable tracking, word-frequency extraction, and QA. Both benchmarks gain question-agnostic compression scenarios. v3's separate extreme-length needle-retrieval sweep is removed.

E2.justification: H2O participates in v3's LongBench comparisons but is absent from v4's evaluated baselines. SnapKV, Pyramid, StreamingLLM, and full-cache references remain; SLM is a table abbreviation for StreamingLLM. The computational-efficiency comparison also drops Pyramid and Ada-Pyramid, retaining SnapKV and Ada-SnapKV.

E3.justification: v4 replaces LWM-Text-Chat-1M with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, adopts GQA-compatible implementations, and changes alpha from 0.5 to 0.2. LongBench adds a 2048-entry average head budget; RULER uses 16K inputs and 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% budgets. Question-agnostic evaluation compresses before supplying questions. LongBench metrics and sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Paired question-aware and question-agnostic evaluations newly stress-test dependence on knowing the query during eviction. The earlier needle-depth and extreme-context-length analysis disappears. The Qasper loss diagnostic also changes from Mistral at 5%/10% cache retention to Llama-3.1 at 20%/40% (v3 Figure 4; v4 Figure 3).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averages across examples or tasks remain point estimates rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds RULER and question-agnostic results, replaces LWM results, and revises retained Mistral results. At 128 entries per head, Mistral's SnapKV/Ada-SnapKV averages change from 35.09/36.71 in v3 Table 1 to 34.55/35.48 in v4 Table 3. These are revised-condition results because GQA handling and safeguard settings change, not direct same-setting performance losses.

T1.justification: v4 strengthens v3 Theorem 4's comparison against uniform allocation to optimality over all budget allocations in Theorem 3.3. The underlying L1 bound and attention-renormalization derivation remain. The expanded Top-k proof introduces an error in Equation 40, writing a minimum where the preceding maximization argument requires a maximum.

C1.justification: The principal claims of adaptive head-level allocation, theoretical grounding, and plug-and-play integration survive. v4 extends the claimed applicability to compression without known questions and emphasizes particular advantages there, replacing v3's emphasis on extreme-length needle retrieval.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly acknowledges that a tighter upper bound does not guarantee lower actual eviction loss and explains how question-agnostic compression relates to prompt caching and multi-turn dialogue. Appendix A.1 removes v3's assertion that further quantization offers limited benefits at 16-bit precision and adds discussion of applying adaptive allocation to dynamic sparsity.

D1.justification: v4 adds extensive prompt templates identifying the question text withheld during compression, plus details of grouped attention selection and variable-length FlashAttention integration. It also provides links to reported external integrations. Conversely, v3's single A100-80G GPU and 16-bit inference disclosures disappear. The original Ada-KV code link remains.

R1.justification: The sliding-window versus Top-k positioning remains. v4 adds references and discussion concerning GQA, FlashAttention-2, RULER, KVPress, prompt caching, SGLang, KIVI, and MInference, while removing LWM and earlier attention-head-analysis references. This updates the surrounding context without redefining the central novelty.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological exposition, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Head heterogeneity moves into the opening motivation, implementation receives a separate subsection, and experiments are reorganized around RULER, LongBench, and computational efficiency. Appendix material is substantially reordered and expanded.

P2.justification: v3's eviction cartoon and needle-retrieval heatmaps disappear, while head-concentration visualization moves to the opening page. v4 introduces numerous RULER panels, reorganizes LongBench tables by model and scenario, combines and moves efficiency plots into the main text, and adds color-coded prompt tables within a single-column appendix layout.

improvement.justification: The new question-agnostic tests strengthen evidence about practical applicability, while GQA-compatible comparisons, explicit prompt templates, and the qualification of the loss-bound guarantee improve relevance, reproducibility, and interpretation. These gains are partly offset by removal of extreme-length retrieval validation and hardware/precision disclosures, together with the introduced min/max error in Equation 40.
